$comment: BC Transit's Kelowna Regional Transit System, published by BC Transit through Consat (tmix.se) as operator 47 (https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/, checked 2026-10-14). Which routes are drawn: routes.json. Regions showing it: central-okanagan. Terms: https://www.bctransit.com/open-data/terms-of-use/ (identify BC Transit as the source; no use of its marks).
name: BC Transit (Kelowna)

static.$comment: Regenerated daily with a new feed_version (e.g. "202610140/20261013 21:00:00/20261014 04:00:00") even when the timetable is unchanged, so fetch-gtfs archives a version only when its files differ from the newest archived one. No dated history. Uses calendar_dates.txt only (no calendar.txt), shape_dist_traveled in metres. How often the timetable really changes: config/regions/central-okanagan/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #1.

realtime.$comment: No API key and no stated request limit. Every bus in the system, with its trip; fixes were p50 ~8 s old when fetched (2026-10-14). Polled within a modest budget all the same: config/regions/central-okanagan/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #2.
realtime.$poll: Guess, to be polite to a provider that states no limit: positions every 30 s while buses run (05:00-24:00), every 60 s overnight; trip updates (~0.25-0.85 MB each) every 2 minutes, 5 overnight; alerts every 5 minutes, 15 overnight. About 3,460 requests a day; dailyCap is a safety net. OPEN-QUESTIONS #2.
realtime.$staleGraceS: Clients fall back to schedule estimates once live data is this much older than the positions poll interval (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate between two fixes at most the positions poll interval plus this apart (guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).
realtime.$extrapolateSlackS: Predict a bus forward for at most the positions poll interval plus this (fixes are fresher than TransLink's: p50 ~8 s, max ~60 s old when fetched; guess, OPEN-QUESTIONS #2).

display.$tripId: Trip ids are three internal ids, <journey>:<variant>:<block> (e.g. 11898518:14545024:14591755); the journey alone is unique on any date (feed of 2026-10-14: a journey appears in at most two trips, never running the same day).
display.$feedVersion: Versions look like "202610140/20261013 21:00:00/20261014 04:00:00": the export date and a sequence number, then the export window.
